director.title:
From TV writer to tango dancer,
Director Lee In-kyung
director.story:
In 2004, as a TV writer, she backpacked to Argentina for 3 months.
What she saw in Buenos Aires!
Citizens blocking an 8-lane road in front of the presidential palace, enjoying music, dance, and human connection until dawn.

"Korea needs this kind of healthy popular culture!"
With that thought, she organized the Daejeon Tango Festival outdoors,
and in 2009, El Tango in Gangnam was born.
director.achievements:
10 training trips to Argentina,
Organizer of De Coreanas Tango Festival,
Former president of Korea Argentine Tango Association,
Champion at the 2023 Rome Tango Competition with her husband and partner~

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Can I learn even if I have no rhythm?
faq.a1: Most El Tango students are complete beginners. Our classes start from walking, balance, rhythm, and communication fundamentals. Your body line improves and balance gets better, correcting your posture. Many are first-time dancers in their 40s, office workers, and couples.
faq.a2: 70% of students come alone. Senior helpers will partner with you, so don't worry. Couples can take class together without partner rotation.
faq.a3: Comfortable clothing and clean indoor shoes are all you need. Budget jazz shoes work great too. Men are encouraged to wear a neat shirt as a courtesy for partner dancing.
